research_basis: brief.md only; plan unreleased at time of this freeze

sources.title: WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format
sources.version_commit: W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft, 2026-05-20; explicitly work in progress
sources.observed_operation: Opened W3C published-version page and inspected status, cue examples, cue ordering/timing, normalization, cue settings and render behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: One data kind per WebVTT file. Cue start offsets are nondecreasing and each cue end is after its start; examples permit overlapping cues. Processing must not normalize Unicode. Rendering/styling support is user-agent limited; regions default to three lines and can clip overflow.
sources.applicability: Per-track timed-text interchange, overlap semantics, rich cue text retention, and export loss reporting. Because this is a CR Draft, treat its status as draft and verify target interoperability before shipping.

sources.title: Timed Text Markup Language 2 (TTML2)
sources.version_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2018-11-08, first edition
sources.locator: Abstract and status; §5 profiles; time expressions and timing parameters; §6 styling vocabulary
sources.observed_operation: Opened the pinned Recommendation and reviewed the abstract/status; inspected the latest-linked document for profiles and timing semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: TTML is timed text intended for interchange among authoring systems. Profile declarations constrain vocabulary/processor behavior. Time expression meaning depends on governing time base, with media as default when unspecified in the inspected specification.
sources.applicability: Richer timed-text alternative; profile-specific implementation and round-trip tests are required. Do not claim every TTML profile or extension is supported.

sources.title: TTML2 Second Edition Candidate Recommendation Snapshot
sources.version_commit: W3C Candidate Recommendation snapshot, 2020-01-28; status text says work in progress
sources.locator: Abstract; §5 profiles; time-expression syntax and frame/tick/time-base conditions
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened the dated W3C snapshot; compared its status and timing model with the pinned first-edition Recommendation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Timed text supports different clock/frame/offset expressions; frame interpretation depends on frame-rate parameters and time base. Draft status is not equivalent to an endorsed final Recommendation.
sources.applicability: Discovery of timing/profile complexity and candidate adapter coverage; not sufficient alone to promise stable 2e support.

sources.title: EPUB 3.3
sources.version_commit: W3C Recommendation, 2026-01-13
sources.locator: §7.2 Media Overlays; OCF §4.2–4.3 path and ZIP physical container
sources.observed_operation: Opened pinned W3C Recommendation and reviewed status, package/container examples and media-overlay description.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Single-file ZIP container includes package documents and resources. Media Overlay synchronizes pre-recorded audio with structured text. OCF defines a virtual common root and path restrictions; EPUB also has remote-resource concepts that do not require this product to fetch them.
sources.applicability: Mature package/manifest and synchronized-text comparator; EPUB remains publication/book oriented and should not be mistaken for the product's native lesson schema.

sources.title: Matroska Element Specification
sources.version_commit: Living official technical specification; page exposes Matroska element versions v1–v4 but no dated release snapshot
sources.locator: Track/TrackEntry, TrackType, TrackUID, FlagDefault, FlagForced, FlagOriginal, Attachments
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official element table and reviewed the track and attachment definitions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: TrackEntry may repeat; track identity, media type, default/forced and related flags are explicit. FlagDefault is eligibility for automatic selection, not a user-visible guarantee; FlagForced applies to subtitle tracks.
sources.applicability: Useful single-clip media-container export/import alternative and track metadata source. Container selection behavior still depends on player policy.

sources.title: Matroska Specification Notes
sources.version_commit: Living official specification notes; no dated release snapshot shown
sources.locator: Track Flags and Default Track Selection
sources.observed_operation: Opened official explanatory notes and searched default/forced semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default flag is a hint that may be overridden by player preferences; forced subtitles can be selected for matching languages even when subtitles would otherwise be disabled.
sources.applicability: Warns against assuming default flags fully express product selection intent; preserve original flags and explain player-dependent behavior.

sources.title: EAF Annotation Format 3.0 and ELAN
sources.version_commit: Official EAF format reference, version 3.0; search result identifies a publication about nine years before access; exact day not displayed
sources.locator: UML model; HEADER/MEDIA_DESCRIPTOR; TIME_ORDER/TIME_SLOT; TIER and annotation types
sources.observed_operation: Searched the official MPI/ELAN source and read available extracted PDF content; the final direct PDF reopen timed out.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: EAF has tier hierarchy and alignable/reference annotations; one shared TIME_ORDER stores time slots across tiers. TIME_VALUE is optional for anchors and ELAN assumes milliseconds. MEDIA_DESCRIPTOR links one or more primary media sources by URI.
sources.applicability: Language annotation alternative with meaningful tier/dependency semantics. It is not a self-contained media package; treat linked resources as local unresolved references unless user selects them.

sources.title: ELAN Media Files and Annotation Files
sources.version_commit: Current official ELAN manual page; no version identifier displayed
sources.locator: Media files and annotation files section
sources.observed_operation: Opened current official manual and inspected the saved-media/annotation-file statement.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Tier setup, alignment and annotations are saved in the EAF/imported annotation file, not in the linked media file.
sources.applicability: Supports separation of annotation model from original media asset and motivates preserving both.

sources.title: ELAN Tier model
sources.version_commit: Current official ELAN manual page; no version identifier displayed
sources.observed_operation: Opened current official manual search result/page.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Tiers may be independent/time-alignable, subdivided, symbolic, or associated with a parent tier; constraints change what a flat subtitle-track model can preserve.
sources.applicability: Useful candidate internal-model precedent; importing to simpler tracks requires a feature/loss report or original retention.

sources.title: Praat TextGrid
sources.version_commit: Current official Praat manual page; no version identifier displayed
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened the official Praat manual.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: TextGrid contains multiple tiers; interval tiers are sequences of labeled intervals and point tiers are labeled points.
sources.applicability: Useful focused alternative for word/phonetic alignment, not package/media interchange.

sources.title: Praat TextGrid file formats
sources.version_commit: Current official Praat manual page; no version identifier displayed
sources.locator: TextGrid file formats and text encoding sections
sources.observed_operation: Searched and read the official format manual excerpt.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Text format permits comments ignored by Praat, has weak/strong invariants, and legacy files use various encodings.
sources.applicability: An importer should validate known invariants, report encoding choice and retain original source rather than assume all readers behave like Praat.

sources.title: Python zipfile — Work with ZIP archives
sources.version_commit: CPython/Python documentation 3.14.8; versioned stable documentation
sources.locator: ZipFile.infolist/open § duplicate names; extract/extractall warnings; Path sanitization note; testzip; compression support
sources.observed_operation: Opened versioned official docs and inspected archive enumeration, duplicate access, path and CRC methods.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Duplicate ZIP member names are supported and callers can use ZipInfo to address them. extract/extractall attempt path sanitation but warn to inspect untrusted archives; zipfile.Path does not sanitize. testzip reads all members for CRC/header checks. ZIP64 and multiple compression methods have version compatibility conditions.
sources.applicability: Implementation evidence for preflight, duplicate-entry disambiguation and limits. The docs do not supply a product-specific safe quota or make any archive universally safe.

sources.title: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format
sources.version_commit: RFC 8259, December 2017
sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor text and inspected JSON object interoperability requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Object member names SHOULD be unique; receiver behavior for duplicates can diverge.
sources.applicability: If a manifest is JSON, reject duplicate keys during parsing rather than silently selecting one interpretation.

sources.title: UTF-8, a transformation format of ISO 10646
sources.version_commit: RFC 3629, November 2003
sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor text and inspected valid-sequence and invalid-sequence rules.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: UTF-8 has constrained valid octet sequences; invalid sequences must not be silently treated as valid encoding.
sources.applicability: Decode with explicit supported-encoding policy, preserve original bytes and report offsets/choice; don't substitute silently.

sources.title: Tags for Identifying Languages
sources.version_commit: RFC 5646 / BCP 47, September 2009
sources.locator: §2 language tag syntax; §2.1 case-insensitivity; §3.1 construction and registry
sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor text and inspected language-tag syntax and construction guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Language tags identify languages using subtags and are case-insensitive; registry-backed preferred forms may evolve.
sources.applicability: Store a normalized validated tag separately from source/display labels and preserve original tag bytes/value for round-trip.

sources.title: FFmpeg WebVTT demuxer source
sources.version_commit: FFmpeg release tag n9.0.2
sources.locator: webvtt_read_header around cue parsing and packet fields; demuxer registration
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged upstream implementation source; inspected WebVTT header/STYLE/REGION/NOTE branch, timestamp parser, cue side data and stream timebase.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Implementation uses a 1/1000 stream timebase; STYLE, REGION and NOTE chunks are skipped in the demux loop; cue identifier/settings are stored as side data. Failed timestamp parsing breaks the read loop. This is FFmpeg n9.0.2 behavior, not a universal WebVTT rule.
sources.applicability: Adapter behavior should be tested against chosen code/version and mapped to explicit diagnostics/loss accounting.

sources.title: FFmpeg SubRip muxer source
sources.version_commit: FFmpeg release tag n9.0.2
sources.locator: ff_srt_muxer output-format declaration and packet writer
sources.observed_operation: Opened tagged upstream source and inspected muxer capability flags.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Muxer declares a maximum of one stream of each type; its implementation writes timestamped event text to one SubRip output.
sources.applicability: If multiple tracks are exported as SRT, create explicit per-track sidecars or choose another package/container; do not imply one SRT file contains a multi-track lesson.

sources.title: FFmpeg command-line documentation
sources.version_commit: Current online documentation at review time; no versioned URL visible and page warns behavior may change with development
sources.locator: §4 Stream selection; §5.11 metadata mapping; disposition options
sources.observed_operation: Opened official online docs and inspected stream-selection, metadata and disposition defaults.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Without -map, FFmpeg chooses one acceptable stream per type, subtitles generally first matching; manual map includes only mapped streams. Global metadata defaults to first input; disposition copying/default selection has conditions.
sources.applicability: If an adapter uses FFmpeg, map every user-selected stream explicitly and compare before/after metadata; do not rely on defaults.

sources.title: FFmpeg-devel WebVTT parser discussion
sources.version_commit: Mailing-list message dated 2025-06-10; patch/discussion history
sources.locator: Message body on header probing, parse tolerance and STYLE/REGION placement
sources.observed_operation: Opened primary FFmpeg developer mailing-list archive.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Discussion records disagreement over strict standards parsing versus accepting malformed/extra content; the message is opinion/review, not proof the patch merged.
sources.applicability: Treat parser strictness as an explicit compatibility decision; preserve source and show malformed/unsupported diagnostics.

sources.title: FFmpeg muxer one-stream-per-type history
sources.version_commit: FFmpeg cvslog commit discussion, March 2024
sources.locator: Change record for MAX_ONE_OF_EACH and SRT single-subtitle restriction
sources.observed_operation: Opened primary FFmpeg commit log archive.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Change introduced a generic maximum-one-stream-of-each-type muxer flag; commit identifies SRT as supporting one subtitle stream.
sources.applicability: Concrete implementation history for the SRT multi-track limitation; do not extrapolate to every SRT tool or format.
